title: A sparse array one cell over the budget is refused, not truncated
rationale: The boundary from above, and the whole reason the bound exists. Nine cells against a budget of eight is REFUSED, not truncated. Truncation was rejected deliberately: dropping columns past a budget leaves every surviving column exactly the right length, so no downstream length check - not AvroReconstructor's ArrayCardinalityException, not agreedElementCount - could see that whole fields had vanished. That is the defect class of the 2.1.0 alignment repair reproduced on purpose, and a refusal is the only outcome that cannot be silent.
catchesBugClass: Any future softening of the refusal into a truncation, and any change that makes the refusal untyped - the exception must stay a FlattenLimitExceededException and must not be rewrapped by flatten()'s catch(Exception) arm.
cannotCatch: It cannot show the resource cost the bound exists to prevent; that is measured by MapFlattenerArrayCellBudgetTest against a 20,000,000-cell document, which is too large to be a fixture.

predicted.detail: REFUSED. Nine cells against a budget of eight throws MapFlattener.FlattenLimitExceededException before any column is allocated. Classified ACCEPTED_LOSS because the refusal is the designed behaviour and the caller is told exactly what happened and which knob to move - a loud, attributable failure rather than a silent one.
